h1: Rattana's Resort Ranong — a little garden home a 5-minute walk from the hot spring
intro: If you're in Ranong to soak at Raksa Warin Hot Spring and want a quiet garden stay rather than a big hotel block, Rattana's Resort is a small garden home of around 6 rooms within a 5-minute walk of the springs · Open since 2010, it sits among shady trees, with spacious rooms that have balconies, a restaurant, a spa and free parking — from around ฿650/night · Real guest reviews adore the owner and the setting, but you should go in knowing the rooms aren't always perfectly kept.

body.html: Rattana's Resort is a small garden resort tucked into Soi Thara in Bang Rin, just a few minutes' walk from Raksa Warin Hot Spring · It has been open since 2010 and holds only about 6 rooms — this is not a big hotel block but an owner-run garden home, surrounded by trees and quiet · Most guests are travellers here to soak at the hot springs, or passing through Ranong before heading on to Koh Phayam, Koh Chang Ranong, or across to Myanmar.

Rooms range from a Double Room (26 sqm, large bed) up to a Family Room with balcony and a Studio with mountain view · What guests agree on is that the rooms are more spacious than you'd expect at this price, and nearly all have a balcony onto the garden · Beds are comfortable, the air-con is cold, and there's a fridge and the basics · That leafy garden-home feel is something you simply won't get from a hotel in town.

"Peaceful spot, loads of trees, an easy walk to the hot spring, and the owner is incredibly kind and helpful with everything — the room was bigger than I expected too. Genuinely good value at this price."

The thing every review mentions most is the genuinely warm owner and staff · Many describe being welcomed like a friend visiting home — the owner suggests places to go, helps book tours, and chats until you feel at ease · There's an on-site restaurant serving both Thai and Russian dishes, and breakfast earns praise for taste · A small spa offers massage, and bicycles are available to ride around the area.

Location is the main strength · It's about a 5-minute walk to Raksa Warin Hot Spring, the free natural mineral baths that are Ranong's signature draw · It's close to the bus station and town, with easy onward transport to the pier for Koh Phayam · The trade-offs are a fairly narrow access lane, and that as a small resort with limited staff, you may sometimes have to wait for the owner.

To be honest, per real guest sentiment: scores here swing widely, from 1 to 10, because room condition isn't consistent · The good reviews talk about clean rooms and a lovely owner; the bad ones describe rooms that weren't kept up — air-con that's hard to start and adjust, a damp, musty bathroom, bedding that isn't always fresh, and weak Wi-Fi throughout · This is an older small resort that needs a bit of TLC. Guests who understand that tend to be happy; those expecting a brand-new hotel standard can be let down.

In short, if you want a quiet, budget-friendly garden home within walking distance of the hot spring, and you value an owner who looks after you like family — Rattana's Resort delivers that feeling at a price that's hard to find · Just book a free-cancellation rate, read the latest reviews, and accept that housekeeping won't be as crisp as a chain · It suits laid-back travellers who care more about atmosphere and people than spotless rooms.

A tip from following the reviews here: message the owner before you arrive to request a freshly cleaned room with the air-con checked · The owner replies quickly and is happy to help — flag that you care about cleanliness and you'll usually get a better-kept room · And if you're going to the hot spring, head over early morning or evening when it's quieter and the air is just right.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Rattana's Resort Ranong

faq.q: Where is Rattana's Resort in Ranong, and is it near the hot spring?
faq.a: Rattana's Resort is at 127/35 Soi Thara, Bang Rin, Mueang Ranong, in the Raksa Warin Hot Spring area · It's about a 5-minute walk to the hot spring, roughly 5 minutes by car to the bus station and 7 minutes to town · It's around 15 minutes from the pier for Koh Phayam and about 30 minutes from Ranong Airport.

faq.q: How much does Rattana's Resort cost, and what rooms are available?
faq.a: Rates start at around ฿650/night for a Double Room (26 sqm) · A Studio with mountain view runs about ฿750, a Triple Room around ฿850, and a Family Room with Balcony around ฿1,000 · Prices vary by date and platform — compare Agoda, Booking and Trip.com before booking.

faq.q: Does Rattana's Resort have a pool? What facilities are there?
faq.a: There is no swimming pool — it's a small garden resort · It has a restaurant serving Thai and Russian food, a massage spa, free parking, Wi-Fi and bicycle rental · The main draws are the quiet garden setting and the walking-distance hot spring.

faq.q: Who is Rattana's Resort best for?
faq.a: It's ideal for laid-back travellers visiting Raksa Warin Hot Spring who want a quiet, budget-friendly garden stay · It suits people who value a friendly owner over a flawless room · It's not for those after a crisp, modern hotel standard, or anyone who needs reliable Wi-Fi for work.

faq.q: Are the rooms at Rattana's Resort clean? Anything to watch for?
faq.a: Reviews swing — some rooms are clean, others aren't kept up well, with mentions of musty bathrooms, bedding that isn't always fresh, and noisy air-con · It's best to message the owner ahead to request a freshly cleaned room, read the latest reviews, and book a free-cancellation rate.

faq.q: Is it easy to reach Koh Phayam from Rattana's Resort?
faq.a: Yes · The resort is near town and the bus station, and it's about 15 minutes by car to the Ranong pier for Koh Phayam · The owner can suggest and help arrange tours and ferry tickets, and many guests stay here before crossing to Koh Phayam or Koh Chang Ranong.
